sender.en: A new match on a dating app or social media

name.en: Romance scam: an online partner who needs money or has an investment tip

how.en: Someone you meet on a dating app or social media builds a close relationship over weeks or months. They soon want to move to WhatsApp or another private app and find reasons not to meet. Later they mention a money problem, hoping you will offer to help, or casually recommend an investment that turns out to be fake. They may also ask for intimate photos that can later be used for blackmail.

text.en: A new match or friend online is very attentive and builds trust over weeks or months.
They ask to move the chat to WhatsApp or another private app and avoid meeting in person.
They mention a money problem, or recommend an investment opportunity.
They may ask for intimate photos.
I feel so close to you even though we have never met. I wish I could come see you but my contract overseas has been extended. Can we talk on WhatsApp instead? I trust only you.
My love, I am so embarrassed to tell you this, but my bank account is frozen and I need to pay the customs fee today. I will pay you back as soon as I get home.

en: They want to move off the dating app quickly.
They always have a reason not to meet or video call.
A money problem comes up, or an investment tip.
They ask you to keep the relationship to yourself.
Never send money to someone you have only met online.
Tell friends or family about a new online relationship.
Don’t share intimate photos or private details you wouldn’t post publicly.
If you have sent money, contact your bank straight away and report it to Police.

story.en: In February 2026 Police arrested an Auckland woman over an alleged romance scam that began online in 2006. Police allege a Dunedin man lost $525,537 over about 18 years.
